title: ces-tester demo:show run report
description: One JSON artifact per operator `demo:show` run, written to runs/show/<runId>/report.json. It exists so deck content can be iterated on evidence rather than recollection: declared vs actual dwell per slide, how the operator moved, and what each op actually did. `demo:show --check` NEVER writes one — this is an operator-run artifact. This schema IS the documentation for the format.

schemaVersion.description: Bumped only when a consumer would break. Additive optional fields do not bump it.

runId.description: The run's identity, and the name of the directory holding this report and every screenshot it references.

startedAt.description: ISO-8601 UTC. When runShow began, before the deck loaded.

endedAt.description: ISO-8601 UTC. When the run ended, BEFORE teardown — a crash in teardown must not cost the report.

exitReason.description: How the run ended. `key` = the operator pressed Esc/q or clicked exit; `signal` = SIGINT/SIGTERM; `error` = a fatal error in the runner. `end-of-deck` is reserved and NOT currently produced: the last slide is a wall, not a wrap (show-state.ts `next`), so a deck never exits itself — a run always ends by key, signal or error.

path.description: The deck path exactly as the operator supplied it.

rowCount.description: Total narration rows across the deck — a slide may span several.

warnings.description: Every load-time warning, carried forward verbatim, so a report explains a deck that opened imperfectly.

run.description: How the run was configured and how the operator drove it.

defaultDwellSec.description: --default-dwell, the fallback for a slide with a blank duration cell.

slidesPort.description: The port the slides server bound. 0 means an ephemeral port was requested — legal, and what the tests use.

autoInitial.description: Auto-pacing at the START of the run. It is toggleable mid-run, so this is an initial value, never the whole truth — see `toggles`.

presenterInitial.description: Presenter band visible at the START of the run. Toggleable mid-run — see `toggles`.

toggles.description: Every mid-run auto/presenter toggle, in order. Recorded as events because a single boolean would misreport any run where the operator pressed `t` or `a`.

manualAdvances.description: How many slide transitions came from an explicit next/prev rather than the auto-pacing tick. High counts mean the deck's declared durations are wrong.

slides.description: One entry per deck slide, in deck order, whether or not it was ever visited.

slideNumber.description: The `slide #` the author typed in Excel.

declaredDurationSec.description: The slide's own `duration (sec)`, or null when that cell was blank.

effectiveDurationSec.description: declaredDurationSec, or the run default when it was blank. This is what the deck ASKED for.

actualDwellMs.description: What the slide actually GOT, summed across every visit. Compare against effectiveDurationSec to retime a deck.

visits.description: Every time this slide was on screen. A slide can be revisited by back-arrow or jump, so this is a list, not one pair.

advance.description: How this visit ended. `auto` = the pacing tick; `manual` = next/prev; `jump` = first/last/goto; `end` = the run ended on this slide.

ops.description: One entry per op DISPATCH, in start order. A staged slide never dispatches, so it never appears here.

opId.description: The registered op id the deck named.

mode.description: live | warm. `staged` ops are never dispatched.

params.description: The op's declared parameters as resolved from the deck. Optional: it is emitted as {} until the params column exists.

endedAt.description: null when the run ended while the op was still in flight.

status.description: `running` means the run ended before the op did — that is a real, reportable outcome, not a gap.

error.description: The failure message, verbatim, when status is `failed`.

artifacts.description: Evidence the op produced — screenshots, execution reports, readiness JSON. Paths are RELATIVE to the tester root, because a report is read on a different machine than it was written on.
